title: Hybrid chunked allocator + live-gap compaction for KV cache
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement:
GPU KV cache fragmentation under continuous batching causes two observable problems: (1) higher effective memory use and premature OOMs when many mid-sized prefixes coexist, (2) bursty latency when bulk evictions occur during rollouts. Existing slab-only and buddy allocators either waste space for many small prefixes or produce large holes for long-lived contexts.

Proposal summary:
Implement a hybrid chunked allocator that mixes small fixed-size chunks for short-lived/prefix-heavy workloads and variable-length windows for long-lived contexts, combined with a low-latency, online "live-gap compaction" mechanism that opportunistically coalesces adjacent free ranges during low-utilization micro-windows detected by the continuous-batching controller. The allocator is designed to: (a) minimize per-request allocation latency, (b) keep fragmentation entropy low, and (c) allow background compaction without violating tail-latency SLOs.

Technical approach (high level):
1) Chunk classes: maintain 3 chunk classes on GPU: small (1–8KB) for token prefixes and short KV entries, medium (8–64KB) for common attention windows, and large (>=64KB) reclaimed into variable windows for long KV sequences.
2) Fast path allocation: continuous-batching threads allocate from per-stream chunk caches to avoid global locks. On miss, a quick bitset-first-fit chooses contiguous chunks up to a cap.
3) Live-gap compaction: runtime monitors per-device idle intervals using the batching scheduler. When an idle micro-window is detected, the compactor attempts to coalesce adjacent free chunks into bigger contiguous windows by issuing GPU memcpy-style move ops that are scheduled with lower priority to avoid interfering with inference kernels. Compaction work is limited by a per-device compaction budget (bytes/sec and max concurrent moves) to control jitter.
4) Heuristics: rank compaction candidates by fragmentation_gain = (coalesced_size - sum(individual_free))/move_cost * reuse_score. Reuse_score is derived from prefix access histograms and TTL estimates maintained by the KV metadata layer.
5) Fallback eviction: if compaction budget is exhausted or fragmentation still prevents allocation, evict low-quality keys using a quality-scored TTL-LRU hybrid to preserve high-value prefixes.
6) Telemetry: emit fragmentation_entropy, avg_free_run_length, compaction_bytes, compaction_moves, compaction_latency_p95, and allocation_failure_rate. Expose dashboards and alert when allocation_failure_rate > 0.1% for >5m.

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- Why hybrid chunks? Pure slab wastes space for long contexts; buddy allocators produce larger external fragmentation. Hybrid chunks allow small cheap allocations and coalescing for large windows.
- Why move-based compaction? GPU kernels can memcpy ranges faster than re-encoding/evicting cached KV; moving preserves warm KV and reduces downstream model recomputation.
- Limiting compaction budget prevents compaction-induced tail latency spikes at cost of slower recovery of fragmentation.

Simulation / bench results (preliminary):
- Memory reclaimed vs baseline slab allocator: +12% on mixed workload trace (production-like 80/15/5 short/mid/long prefix mix).
- OOM events reduced: -18% in stress runs (10k concurrent streams).
- Compaction cost: average 2.2ms per 256KB coalesce move; p95 stays <8ms under budgeted background priority.
- Observed p95 token latency increase during aggressive compaction tests: +6% without bandwidth throttling; with throttle (recommended) impact <1%.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement allocator and unit tests behind feature flag. Run microbenchmarks on staging.
2) Canary on a small Dedicated pool with compaction disabled (to validate allocation correctness + telemetry).
3) Enable compaction in canary with conservative budget; run for 48h.
4) Gradually increase compaction budget and sample workloads.
5) Full rollout to runtime-1.21 after sign-off and dashboarding.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: compaction moves could collide with KV readers/writers -> mitigation: use fine-grained per-chunk locking and schedule moves at low priority; expose kernel scheduling hooks to avoid contention.
- Risk: inaccurate reuse_score leads to wasted compaction -> mitigation: warm-up reuse models from production telemetry and fall back to simple age-based heuristics if confidence low.
- Risk: cross-device migration complexity -> mitigation: compaction limited to device-local coalescing; cross-device balance handled by higher-level routing and shard placement changes.

Acceptance criteria and success metrics are listed separately.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Allocator passes synthetic allocation correctness suite (no data corruption, per-chunk lock invariants hold).
2) Fragmentation_entropy reduced by >=10% vs current slab allocator on mixed trace within 24h steady-state.
3) Allocation_failure_rate <= 0.05% in canary under production-like load with compaction enabled.
4) p99 token latency impact from compaction <= 2% under normal load (measured over 30d canary).
5) Dashboards for compaction_bytes, fragmentation_entropy, allocation_failures, compaction_latency_p95 live in Grafana with runbook linked.
6) PRs merged with unit + integration tests and documented Confluence design doc.

2026-01-08 - David Park: Prototype allocator implemented; local bench shows 9% memory reclamation on mixed trace. Found a race in per-stream cache refill path; added a small fix. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rf-runtime/pull/4291

2026-02-24 - Design review (Ruth Chen): UX for compaction toggle and per-customer knobs approved. Need to add opt-out flag for Private deployments. Added label 'customer-opt-out'.
